issues.legal_issue: A partly built parcel is subject to the ceiling computation even when the holder does not own a separate vacant parcel, and land appurtenant to a building means land forming part of the same plot as the building.
material_facts: The landholder possessed one parcel containing both a building and open land and sought permission to sell part of the open land.

The lower courts treated the appurtenant-land provisions as requiring a distinct vacant parcel, while the Supreme Court considered whether the open land had to be held separately from the plot containing the building.
issues.conclusion: The distinct-parcel requirement was rejected. Section 4(9), read with sections 2(q)(ii) and 2(q)(iii), applies whether or not the landholder owns a separate vacant parcel; appurtenant land is land forming part of the plot containing the building, not merely nearby or contiguous land.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4(9) and 2(q)(ii) and (iii) must be read together. The wording of section 4(9) connects the appurtenant land to the building and the plot on which it stands. The Court applied the principle that a beneficial statute is construed to suppress the mischief and advance its object. It approved M/s. Eastern Oxygen & Acetylene Ltd. v. State of Madhya Pradesh and overruled State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. v. L. J. Johnson & Anr.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: A competent authority is determining how much urban land a holder may retain under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.parcel_partly_built: The holder's parcel has a building on part of it and open land on the remainder.
predicates.open_land_in_same_plot: The open land forms part of the plot containing the building.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns a partly built parcel, open land in the same plot is included in the computation even if the holder has no separate vacant parcel.

issues.legal_issue: In computing the ceiling for a partly built parcel containing a dwelling unit, the built area and qualifying appurtenant allowances are treated in accordance with the statutory exclusions, and any remaining excess is liable to be taken over.
material_facts: The landholder's parcel measured 2,530 square metres and included a building with a stated built area of 464 square metres.
The competent authority refused permission to sell open land on the basis that the total area exceeded the applicable ceiling.
The lower courts allowed exclusions for land required to remain open under local rules and for additional land for beneficial enjoyment of the building, but their computation was rejected.
issues.conclusion: The built area and the allowances permitted for required open space and beneficial enjoyment must be taken into account when computing the ceiling; the whole plot is not exempt merely because it contains a building. The Supreme Court stated that the reported parcel's excess was 530 square metres, while directing fresh computations by the competent authority in the cases before it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(g), 2(q)(ii) and (iii), and 4(9) govern the treatment of land occupied by a qualifying building and land appurtenant to it. The Court held that the landholder may set apart required open space up to the statutory maximum and retain an additional appurtenant area for beneficial use; the remaining area is assessed against the applicable ceiling. The construction follows the Act's purpose of imposing a ceiling without treating qualifying built and appurtenant land as vacant land for acquisition.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: A competent authority is determining how much urban land a holder may retain under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.parcel_partly_built: The holder's parcel has a building on part of it and open land on the remainder.
predicates.qualifying_building_with_dwelling_unit: The parcel contains a building with a dwelling unit that qualifies for the statutory treatment of built and appurtenant land.

issues.definition: For a partly built parcel with a qualifying dwelling-unit building, the built and permitted appurtenant areas are excluded in determining what land remains in excess.

issues.legal_issue: A holder's vacant and partly built plots must be aggregated when determining the applicable ceiling, and the holder may choose which area to retain within that ceiling.
material_facts: The Court considered how to compute the ceiling where a holder had several plots, some entirely vacant and others partly built and partly vacant.
The plots could be in different places, and the Act provided the holder an option to select the area to retain.
issues.conclusion: The competent authority must total the holder's relevant land across the plots, apply the applicable ceiling, and allow the holder to select the area to retain so long as it does not exceed that ceiling.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4(1) and 6 govern the ceiling and the holder's selection of land to retain. The Court held that all relevant plots, whether wholly vacant or partly built and partly vacant, must be totalled before applying the ceiling and the selection option.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: A competent authority is determining how much urban land a holder may retain under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.holder_has_multiple_relevant_plots: The holder possesses more than one relevant plot, whether vacant or partly built and partly vacant.

issues.definition: When a holder has multiple relevant plots, the plots are aggregated for the ceiling computation and the holder may select the retained area within the ceiling.

issues.legal_issue: Where a holder has vacant land in urban agglomerations belonging to different ceiling categories, the ceiling must be determined using the statutory category-based formula.
material_facts: The Court addressed the computation of a holder's vacant land situated in urban agglomerations belonging to two or more categories.
The Act prescribed different ceiling limits for different categories of urban agglomeration.
issues.conclusion: The competent authority must determine the ceiling in accordance with the formula prescribed for holdings in multiple categories.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1)(a) to (d) prescribes the category-based ceiling limits and the formula applicable where vacant land is held in two or more categories of urban agglomeration.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: A competent authority is determining how much urban land a holder may retain under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.vacant_land_in_multiple_ceiling_categori: The holder has vacant land in urban agglomerations assigned to more than one ceiling category.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns vacant land in multiple categories, the category-based formula is applied to determine the ceiling.
